runs.text: It is the environment in which a Java program is loaded and executed. One way to understand it is as the region in RAM used for running a Java application.
2. Why does a Java program need a runtime environment?
A Java program cannot simply be loaded anywhere in memory and executed.
The operating system allocates a specific region in RAM where the Java program and the required execution-related components are loaded.
3. Does every running Java application use its own runtime environment?
Each Java application gets its own runtime environment for execution.
For example, if two Java applications are running, each application has its own allocated execution environment.
4. What is another way to define JRE?

collection of software required to execute a Java program
It is responsible for executing Java bytecode by providing the required execution mechanisms.
6. What important components are present inside the JVM?
These components participate in Java program execution.
It converts Java bytecode into machine-level instructions during execution.
8. What is the role of the Java interpreter?
The Java interpreter also participates in converting or executing bytecode.
Both the interpreter and JIT are involved in converting bytecode into a form that can ultimately be executed by the machine.
9. What is the difference between JIT and the Java interpreter at this level?
Both are involved in handling bytecode and machine-level execution, but they perform that work differently.

10. What is the purpose of the runtime system inside the JVM?
The runtime system supports activities required while the Java program is executing.
Exception-handling support is given as one example of runtime responsibility.
A class loader is a component required during Java execution to load the classes needed by the program.
It is one of the important components used when a Java application runs.
A bytecode verifier checks whether the bytecode is valid Java bytecode and whether it has been improperly modified.
This verification contributes to Java's security.
Java libraries contain predefined functionality that Java programs can use.
Required library code is made available during program execution.

26. What does “Write Once, Run Anywhere” mean in Java?
It means a Java program written and compiled once can run on different systems, provided the required Java execution environment is available.
The same program can run irrespective of geographical location, operating-system platform, or system architecture.
27. Why can the same Java program run on different operating systems?
Java source code is compiled into platform-independent bytecode.
Each operating system uses the JVM appropriate for that platform to execute the bytecode.
Java language and bytecode are platform independent, but the JVM is platform dependent
Different platforms require their corresponding JVM implementations.
29. What does architecture-neutral mean in Java?
Architecture-neutral means the same Java program can execute on machines with different underlying architectures without changing the program, provided the required JVM is available.
The program behaves consistently irrespective of the architecture of the system on which it run
30. What does portability mean in Java?
Portability means a Java program created on one platform can be transported to another platform and executed there.
This is why Java is described as a portable programming language.
